FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indain Standards, after the draft finalized by the Electric Fans Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. Supplies of the railway carriage fans to the Indian Railways have been made in the past on the basis of the 1R specifications for the railway carriage fans. Although there is lot of commonalty between electric fans of ot.her types and the railway carriage fans, the latter are required to withstand rough service conditions with minimum and simple maintenance and also have special mounting design, etc, suitable for railway carriage. With a view of utilizing the experience gained in the formulation of Indian Standard specifications for other types of fans and also the information available at international level, it was decided to formulate Indian Standard for railway carriage fans. This standard was first issued in 1972. This revision has been prepared to take into account the developments taken place since then and to bring the standard in line with the changes already incorporated by Indian Railways. In preparing this specification, the general aspects accepted in the IEC publications have been adopted. Assistance has also been derived from the following: E.4-70 IRS Specification E.4A-58 IRS Specification for carriage fans and regulators for carriage fans and regulators for electric on electric fans

( 24 volts, dc ). Indian Railways. ( 110 volts, dc/ac ). Indian Railways. Part 1 : Fans and regulators shall be `Medium' in

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that ~of the specified value in ?his standard.

1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies the requirements and methods of tests for ac and dc fixed, swivelling and bracket type fans, including the associated speed regulators, for use in railway carriages. It covers the following 24 a> fans: 3.5 Routine Tests Tests carried out on each fan to check the essential requirements which are likely to vary during production. 3.6 Acceptance Tests Tests carried out on samples selected from a lot for the purpose of verifying the acceptability of the lot. 3.6.1 Lot All fans of the same type, and manufactured from same material under similar conditions of production shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 4. SIZES 4.1 Standard sizes of the fans shall be 225, 300 and 400 mm.

V dc fans for conventional 24 V coaching stock; W 110 V dc fans for self generating 110 V coaching stock, and dc electrical multiple units; 110 V ac fans for coaching stock with end-on-generation and mid-on-generation coaches and also for 110 V self-generating coaches and dc EMU stock where invertors or motor alternator sets are provided for 110 V ac 50 cycles feed for working carriage fans; and 4 140 V ac fans for ac electrical multiple units.

2 REFERENCES 2.1 The Indian Standards listed in Annex A are necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3 TERMINOLOGY 3.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions, in addition to those given in IS 1885 ( Part 55 ) : 1981 shall apply. 3.1 Railway Carriage Fans A propeller-bladed fan, unless otherwise specified, having 4 blades directly driven by an electric motor and provided with a device for mounting on wall, ceiling or a bracket and intended for use with free inlet and outlet. .3.2 Extra Low Voltage A nominal voltage not exceeding 42 V between conductors and between conductors and earth, the no-load voltage not exceeding 50 V. 3.3 Cooling Air Temperature The temperature of the surrounding in which the fan operates. .3.4 Type Tests Tests carried out to prove conformity with the requirements of this standard. These are intended to prove general qualities and design of a given type of fan. 1 atmosphere

7 NUMBER OF PHASES

7.1 The ac fans shall have single phase motors. 8 DESIGN AND GENERAL CONSTRUCT-IO& 8.1 The fans shall be of three types, namely, fixed, swivelling and bracket type. Fixed and swivelling type fans shall be of 300 and 400 mm size and bracket type shall be of 225 mm size. The motor unit shall be so designed that it may

IS 6680:1992
be readily dismantled without disturbing the fan base. The fan shall be of robust construction to ensure satisfactory operation under conditions of vibration, rough usages, etc, obtained in the railway carriages. The design shall be generally according to relevant figures. The dimensions and tolerances shown therein for different parts shall be strictly adhered to. The fan motor shall be totally enclosed and of one of the following types: DC motor shall be series wound and shall be provided With an inspection opening of a suitable size with a dust-proof cover to facilitate the inspection of commutator and brushes. AC capacitor type motor shall be so designed that the performance of fans working in dusty atmosphere is not impaired.

8.6 Bearings

The motor shall be fitted with deep groove single row ball bearing ~of approved make with an inner race diameter of 10 mm for all types of fans. The design of the bearing housing shall be such as to permit armature being removed together with the bearings. The outer races of the bearings shall be properly fixed to prevent creepage of the bearing in the housing. Adequate provision shall be made to prevent grease creeping out, alternatively grease sealed bearing shail be provided. The housing shall be of ample capacity to hold sufficient grease for normal working for a period of 4 000 working hours. The nominal dimension of ball bearing shall be 10 mm ( ID ), 30 mm ( OD ), 9 mm ( widths). The bearings shall he of normal class PO tolerance as per IS 5692 : 1988 and normal radial clearances as per IS 5935 : 1970. The bearing designation shall be as per IS 6455 : 1972. Alternatively if agreed between the purchaser and the supplier, the motor shall be fitted with one ball bearing and one plain cylindrical sintered bush bearing, conforming 10 Gr I-B1 ( low density of IS 3980 : 1982 ).

The nominal dimension of bush bearing shall be 3.589f&,ls mm ( ID ), 15-989~&,21 mm ( OD ); 20.6 f O-165 mm ( L ). Provision of additional lubrication by oil soaked felt ring shall be made for the bush bearing. The bush bearing shall be provided at blade end. 8.6.1 Instructions for the proper lubrication nf bearing shall be furnished by the manufacturer. 8.6.2 The bearing retaining screw shall be provided on the commutator end bearing and a suitable lock washer shall be provided to hold the ball bearing in position on blade end side so that armature may be removed together with both the bearings for maintenance. 8.7 Guard The fans shall have a suitable robust guard to provide. in normal use, adequate protection against personal injury as far as possible and shall be of close mesh type unless otherwise specified. When ihe guards are in two pieces positive locking arrangement to keep the two pieces together should be made.

8.7.4 The fans shall have a suitable robust guard to provide adequate protection against personal injury as far as possible in normal use. Only close mesh guards in accordance with Fig. 5 shall be provided. The wires of the guard shall be not less than 1.6 mm in diameter ( see IS 1137 : 1990 ) and the centre distance between the wires shall not exceed 10 mm. 8.9 Method of Mounting 8.9.1 The mounting `Rigid -

8.7.2 In the case of swivelling or bracket type fans, the guard shall be fitted with a suitable hand grip for adjusting the position of the fan. 8.8 Brushes and Brush Holders The dc fans shall be provided with brush holder arrangement as given in Fig. 16. All electrical leads shall terminate in soldered or crimped brass/copper lugs which shall be fixed in position by means of screws. The carbon brush and spring shall be provided in accordance with Fig. 17. The grade of carbon brushes shall be
as agreed between the purchaser and the supplier.

The direction of draught is changed only by changing the position ofthe fan. Motors for such fans shall be secured in the lower hinged position of the frame for convenience of inspection. The dc motor shall be able to swing about the hinge and expose its commutator side so that the commutator and the brushgear may be examined with ease.' 8.9.2 Clamping Devices All clamping devices, where provided, shall be of strong and simple design. Thy shall be so arranged that the mechanism may be positively adjusted without there being undue risk of its. working loose. 8

11.4 The mechanism of the regulator shall be so designed as to ensure positive contact at each running position. 12 STARTING 12.1 The fan shall be capable of starting from rest at 85 percent of the lowest voltage in the voltage range with the regulator, if any, being set in any of the positions of normal use.

FAN REGULATORSWITCH ( THREE SPBBDS )
15.5 The surface roughness of the commutator will not exce-ed roughness value of 5 microns. The commutator shall be of true cylindrical shape without any skew. The ovality on the commutator will not be more than 0.05 mm and the unevenness between the adjacent bars will be within 0.03 mm.

15 COMMUTATORS 15.1 Motors with commutators shall have a fixed brush setting. They shall work from full speed to lowest speed without undue sparking and without injury to the surface of commutator or brushes. 15.2 Commutator bar shall be made of copper of ETP to IS 5885 : 1977. The built up mica or treated mica commutator separator shall be used as per IS 2464 : 1963. 15.3 The commutator shall consist of 24 segments and shall have dia of 40 f O-5 mm. The thickness of the mica separator shall be `0.8 f O-2 mm. 15.4 The radial gap between the commutator and the brush holder shall be maintained between 2-5 f 0.5 mm. Commutator will be with flush mica segments so as to obviate necessity of undercutting, etc, in service.

16 PERFORMANCE

REQUIREMENTS

16.1 The minimum air delivery and the maximum electrical power input at the test voltages and at full speed shall be as given in Table 1. The maximum weight of the complete fan is also specified against each size. 17 TOLERANCES ON RATINGS

17.1 For a railway carriage fan covered by this standard, in no case shall the measured performance be inferior to that given in this standard. 18

For routine tests, industrial cIass measuring instruments may be used ( see IS 1248 ( Parts 2 and 3 ) : 1983. 19.1.5 Test Voltage The voltage at which various tests are to be conducted are given below for 24 V dc, 110 V dc, 110 V ac and 140 V ac fans respectively: r-----.-----24 Vdc 36 V dc 20 V dc 24 V dc 24 V dc Test Voltage For *--_~-_---___~ 110 Vdc 110 V ac 135 V dc 135 V ac 98 V dc 98 V ac 110 V ac 1lOVac 110 V dc 110 V ac 110 v ac

e) Leakage test ( 19.6 ), f ) Al 1 acceptance tests, g) Corrosion test ( under consideration ), and h) High operating voltage test for 24 V dc and 110 V dc fans. The 24 V dc and 110 V dc fans shall be subjected to 45 V dc and 229 V dc for five minutes and shall not show undue wear on brushes or commutator and no damage to the insulation shall occur. 19.1.2 The following shall constitute acceptance tests: a) Starting ( 12 ), b) Air delivery ( 19.2 ), c) High voltage ( 19.7 ), d) Electrical input ( 19.8 ), e) Fan speed ( 19.9 ), and ( 19.11). f ) insulation-resistance 19.1.2.1 Acceptance test, if requested, shall be made on samples selected according to a method of sampling agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. A recommended method of sampling is given in Annex D. 19.1.3 The tests: following shall constitute routine

19.1.5.1 Limits of voltage varitation The variation in the test voltage shall not exceed rt 1 percent of the test voltage during air delivery test. While taking the current and watt readings during these tests, however, the voltage shall be maintained at the test voltage. 19.1.6 Before taking any steps towards testing a fan in accordance with this standard, it is essential that it should have been `run in' for at least one hour at the highest voltage of the voltage range unless otherwise specified. 19.2 Air Delivery Test ( Type Test ) The following method for determining delivery of the fan shall be followed. 19.2.1 Test Chamber The fan shall be tested in a test chamber having the following dimensions: Length : 4.50 m, width : 4.50 m, and height : 3.0 m. This chamber shall extraneous draughts carried out. be reasonably free from while the test is being the air

a) Flash test ( 19.10 ), b) Insulation-resistance

( 19.11), and 20

19.2.1.1 The test chamber sllall be free from obstructions other than the stand on which the fan is mounted. Any table or shelf for electrical instruments shall be on the intake side of the fan, beyond a distance of 0.90 m from the plane

3s 6680 : 1992 of the fan blades. No heating or cooling apparatus shall be used in the test room while the test is in progress. The fan shall be mounted with the blade centre l-20 m from the floor and with the front of the blades at least 1.20 m from the back wall and at least 1.80m from the side walls. 19.2~2 Testing hstrumen t The air movement shall be measured by means of a rotating vane anemometer having an internal diameter not exceeding 100 mm suitable for the range of velocities to be measured. It is that recommended the anemometer be calibrated frequently. 19.2.3 Arrangement of Apparatus 19.2.3.1 The arrangement of the apparatus ( see Fig. 22 ) shall be such as to permit the anemometer being moved in a horizontal plane containing the axis of the fan, the movement being at right angles to the axis and extendable in both directions. The anemometer shall be supported in such a manner as to offer as little obstruction as possible to the air flow. The axis of the anemometer vane shall always be parallel "0 the axis of the fan blades. 19.2.3.2 The distance between the test plane and the plane of the fan blades shall be three times the size of the fan in millimetres. For example: Distance between the test plane and the plane of the fan blades for 300 mm size fan shall be: 3 x 300 = 900 mm 19.2.4 Procedure_for Test 19.2.4.1 The measurements shall be carried out with the fan running at full speed at the test voltage and with the guard in position. 19.2.4.2 Readings shall commence at a point 20 mm from the axis of the fan blades, and shall progress along the horizontal line in each direction, by increments of 40 mm in width. Readings shall be continued in each direction until the true air velocity falls below 24 metres per minute. 19.2.4.3 Each reading shall consist of the time taken by an air movement of 300 m measured by the anemometer, except when such air movement takes more than two minutes; the Teading shall then consist of the time taken ~by a movement of some convenient and readable quantity of air requiring approximately two minutes. In no case should the duration of the reading be less than one minute. 19.2.4.4 The average air velocity over any annulus. shall be the mean of the readings on either side of the axis of the fan blades at each mean radius of annulus. 19.2.4.5 The average velocity so obtained, multiplied by the area of the corresponding, annulus shall be taken as the total air delivery through that annulus.

19.11 Insulations-Resistance Test ( Routine Test )

19.11.1 The insulation-resistance test shall be carried out on fans and regulators immediately after conducting the flash test ( see 19.10 ).

19.11.2 The insulation-resistance of the fan motor and its regulator shall be not less than two megohms when tested after the completion of the flash test, with a de voltage of approximately 500 volts applied between points as used for the high voltage test or flash test.

iii) Stator, and iv) Rotor; Angles of fan adjustment ( for swivelling fans only ); Details of regulator resistance wirers ( size, resistance, weight ); Weight of fan; Drawings showing the overal! dimenGons of the fan including motor unit with fixing centres. OF SAMPLING

The number of fans selected as per co1 1 and 2 of Table 3 shalt be subjected to all the acceptance tests. A fan failing to satisfy any of the requirements of acceptance test shall be termed as defective. The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of acceptance test if the number of defectives in the sample is less than or equal to the corresponding acceptance number ( see cot 4 of Table 3 ). The lot shall be rejected if the number of defectives in the sample is greater than or equal to the corresponding first rejection number ( see co1 5 of Table 3 ). If the number of defective are in between the acceptance number and first rejection number then a second sample of same size ( see co1 3 of Table 3 ) shall be selected from the lot at random and subjected to all the acceptance tests. The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirement of acceptance test if the total number of defectives in the first and second sampie combmed is less than the corresponding second rejection number ( see co1 6 of Table 3 ), otherwise not.

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and -operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
